site.name: Cold Spring Mine
site.location: Trevarton Gulch / Boulder County Tungsten Mining District near Nederland
overview: Cold Spring Mine was a major historic tungsten producer in Boulder County's tungsten district, about two miles northeast of Nederland in Trevarton Gulch.
Colorado mining records document deep multi-level workings, substantial twentieth-century tungsten production, and renewed federal-supported exploration during the 1950s.

timeline.text: Colorado's tungsten-mine inventory recorded 101,586 units of production from ore averaging 7.1 percent and estimated that total production ultimately exceeded 200,000 units.
The mine was reopened under the Defense Minerals Exploration Administration, with extensive core drilling and additional underground development.
A Colorado Supreme Court decision described Cold Spring Tungsten, Inc. as owning a tungsten mine and mill near Nederland while pursuing treatment of low-grade tailings.

moreHistory: Colorado Geological Survey's Tungsten Mines of Colorado places the Cold Spring workings in Sections 7 and 8, Township 1 South, Range 72 West, in Trevarton Gulch about two miles northeast of Nederland. The state inventory describes two shafts reaching about 480 feet with eight underground levels.

The same state source records major historic tungsten production and renewed 1950s exploration under the federal DMEA program, showing that Cold Spring was substantially more than a mapped name or minor prospect.

The Boulder County tungsten-district locality near 39.98333, -105.48333 is used as a defensible mine-level identification point supported by the retained federal/state source trail. It is not presented as a field-surveyed surviving shaft collar or as evidence of current access or safety.
This tungsten property is distinct from the separate Cold Spring gold-mine locality near Gold Hill; the two names should not be combined.
